audio_transcription:
Chat keeps a team conversation with its intended participants. Open the chat button at the bottom of the page where it is available. The widget shows department and group channels, including the synthetic command and squab three groups in our Firehouse 51 department. Those names describe our training organization. A search team can use team groups, a security company site groups, a mobile response service operational teams, a wildland contractor crews, and an industrial department facility groups.
This is separate from the assistant button, which opens an AI assistance conversation. Chat availability depends on the deployed chat feature and department access. In this lesson, the training stack already has it enabled. We do not claim that a learning choice or a module label activates every rollout feature. New conversation opens a member picker. We select only the fictional Matthew Casey and Kelly Severeid. With multiple recipients, the action changes to creative
group and a name field appears. Enter training, field coordination, and create the group. It appears as a conversation with the current sender and the chosen participants. A department wide channel and an explicitly selected conversation are different audience choices. For a security site, consider whether the whole site group needs the message or only the supervisor and assigned patrol. For mobile response, choose the actual operational team. For search, wildland, and industrial response, choose the
people coordinating the current assignment. Group creation is not a dispatch assignment and does not change the member's staffing or unit availability. Enter a concise coordination message. Our synthetic message says team alpha is preparing for a staging area exercise and explicitly separates the message from dispatch. Send message adds it to the conversation with Wallace Bowdoin as sender and a timestamp. Reopening the saved conversation after navigation retains the message.
It proves the message was saved and can be read in this view. It does not prove another device received a push or that the participants read it. Emoji, GIF, and image controls are visible in the composer. Attachments need their own approved content and client test. Keep sensitive personal, clinical, client, and facility details within your organization's approved record and access procedures. A chat conversation is not a substitute for an incident record, a roster declaration, or a formal
instruction that needs a different workflow. For a message that needs an explicit acknowledgement, select send as urgent, requires acknowledgement before sending. Our second message asks the two fictional participants to acknowledge an accountability briefing for this exercise. The result displays U-R-G-E-N-T and zero of two acknowledged. Expanding the count in the widget shows Matthew Casey pending and Kelly Severide pending. The count describes the expected recipients
and recorded acknowledgments for this message. It does not prove operational readiness, completion of an assignment, or independent receipt by a device. Review how your department follows up when someone remains pending. This recording leaves both recipients pending. It does not simulate a recipient's acknowledgement or claim emergency notification delivery. Use reply and thread on the urgent message to keep follow-up with that message. The widget changes to thread, shows the original message, a replies area,
and a composer. We add a synthetic clarification that area alpha is the practice sector. Then send it. The thread now shows one reply. Close thread returns to the main conversation where the original message has a one reply button and still shows zero of two acknowledged. A reply does not perform the message's recipient acknowledgement. The original sender's follow-up also cannot stand in for either recipient. This distinction is useful when a patrol supervisor clarifies a site instruction
a search leader clarifies a sector or an industrial coordinator clarifies a facility access point. Add reaction opens the quick reaction choices. We select thumbs up on the synthetic urgent message. The live view did not immediately show the reaction, so we reload the page and reopen the conversation. The saved result now shows one thumbs up, one reply and zero of two acknowledged. A reaction is separate from the acknowledgement request. This build also displayed clock value
use differently for live and freshly fetched messages. Verify the display before interpreting timestamps as local chronology. The full chat workspace was opened, but at this normal viewport, its message area was compressed and its thread pain was hidden. The widget provided a readable working thread path. This recording uses that observed path and leaves full workspace layout and other client verification as follow-up work. For community paramedics and mental health response, coordinate the operational team and
over while maintaining approved record boundaries. For search and rescue, use team and staging conversations with explicit follow-up for accountability instructions. For security companies, use site and patrol groups with the intended supervisor audience. For wildland contractors, coordinate crew and staging information and review connectivity and fallback procedures. For industrial emergency teams, coordinate facility access, equipment issues and handover with the intended responders.
Your practice exercise is to choose a channel audience, create a small synthetic group, send an ordinary message, request acknowledgement, record a focus thread reply and inspect the separate counts. Reopen the conversation to verify persistence. Then, test authorized recipients on the actual devices and channels used by your organization and record what the training demonstration has not proved.
